account: Today I have my usual appointments: morning office business, a ten-o'clock grain inspection at the mill, lunch at home, council letters at thirteen, tea with my neighbour at fifteen, and office time at sixteen-thirty. The unusual addition is an eighteen-o'clock meeting in the great hall arranged by the innkeeper. He calls it a community hospitality matter, says I should come alone, and insists that no preparation is needed. The secretary has recorded it and will remind and escort me. Yesterday evening I overheard the baker asking the builder how many loaves had reached the hall, where freight was, and about unresolved grain funding. That suggests people are organizing food or hospitality at the hall, possibly for tonight's meeting, although nobody has told me the connection or its precise purpose. It could be a gathering or surprise, but that is only a guess. My neighbour has confirmed our ordinary afternoon tea and has not yet answered my question about town news. No council correspondence has reached the secretary this morning. Town accounts also remain unresolved: I counted 128 emeralds in the treasury yesterday, but we have not located a ledger or identified its custodian. I do not know whether the baker's grain-funding question has any connection to town funds.
